chunks: Ali ibn Hatim from Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn Ahmad ibn Butta al-Qummi from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab from Muhammad ibn Sinan and Abu Muhammad Harun ibn Musa said: We were narrated by Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Ma'mar from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab from Muhammad ibn Sinan from al-Mufaddal ibn Umar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said:

Extra prayers of one thousand rak'ahs are prayed in the month of Ramadan. I said: 'And who can manage that?' He said: 'Not where you go, do you not pray extra of one thousand rak'ahs in the month of Ramadan? Nineteen of them, in each night twenty rak'ahs; and in the night of the nineteenth, one hundred rak'ahs; and in the night of the twenty-first, one hundred rak'ahs; and in the night of the twenty-third, one hundred rak'ahs; and you pray in eight nights of it, in the last ten, thirty rak'ahs. So these are nine hundred and eighty rak'ahs.'

I said: 'May I be your ransom, you have relieved me; the matter had indeed become tight for me, but when you came to me with the explanation, you relieved me. So how is the completion of the thousand rak'ahs?' He said: 'You pray in every Friday during the month of Ramadan four rak'ahs for the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him); and you pray two rak'ahs for the daughter of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family); and after the two rak'ahs, you pray four rak'ahs for Ja'far al-Tayyar; and you pray in the night of Friday during the last ten [nights] for the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) twenty rak'ahs; and you pray in the evening of Friday, the night of Saturday, twenty rak'ahs for the daughter of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family).'

Then he said: 'Listen, pay attention, and teach the trustworthy ones of your brothers these four and the two rak'ahs, for they are the best of prayers after the obligatory ones. Whoever prays them in the month of Ramadan or in other months, he is released, and there is no sin between him and Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.'

Then he said: 'O Mufaddal ibn Umar, you recite in all of these prayers, meaning the extra prayer of the month of Ramadan, with Al-Hamd and Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad. If you wish, once; if you wish, three times; if you wish, five times; if you wish, seven times; if you wish, ten times.'

As for the prayer of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), you recite in it Al-Hamd in each rak'ah, and fifty times 'Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad'. And you recite in the prayer of the daughter of Muhammad (peace be upon her), in the first rak'ah, Al-Hamd and 'Inna anzalnahu fi laylat al-Qadr' one hundred times; and in the second rak'ah, Al-Hamd and 'Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad' one hundred times.

So when you have finished the two rak'ahs with the salutation, glorify with the glorification of Fatimah al-Zahra (peace be upon her), which is: 'Allahu Akbar' thirty-four times, 'Al-hamdu lillah' thirty-three times, and 'Subhanallah' thirty-three times. By Allah, if there were anything better than it, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) would have taught it to her.

And he said to me: 'You recite in the prayer of Ja'far: in the first rak'ah, Al-Hamd and 'Idha zulzilat'; in the second, Al-Hamd and 'Al-Adiyat'; in the third, Al-Hamd and 'Idha ja'a nasr Allah'; and in the fourth, Al-Hamd and 'Qul Huwa Allahu'.'
Then he said to me: 'O Mufaddal, that is the bounty of Allah which He gives to whom He wills, and Allah is the Lord of great bounty.'

key_terms.تَسْبِيحَ فَاطِمَةَ: The glorification of Fatimah (specific dhikr formula)
key_terms.زِيَادَةُ أَلْفِ رَكْعَةٍ: Extra prayers of one thousand rak'ahs
key_terms.صَلَاةُ أَمِيرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Prayer of the Commander of the Faithful (Imam Ali)
key_terms.صَلَاةُ ابْنَةِ مُحَمَّدٍ: Prayer of the daughter of Muhammad (Fatimah)

ai.seo_question: What are the specific extra prayers and their recitations for the month of Ramadan according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* provides a detailed jurisprudential breakdown of the 'Ziyadah' (extra) prayers in Ramadan, totaling one thousand rak'ahs, which are distinct from the widely known Taraweeh. It highlights the specific liturgical practices for prayers dedicated to Imam Ali, Lady Fatima, and Ja'far al-Sadiq, emphasizing that consistent performance of these specific prayers expiates sins, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the spiritual authority of the Ahl al-Bayt in intercession and devotion.
